premises.evidence_span: sites like ACM and Topcoder focus on a small set of textbook algorithms, whereas in the real world, you work on things ranging from machine learning to artificial intelligence to distributed systems

premises.text: HackerRank offers varied challenges across difficulty levels with dynamic ranking based on how many users solve them
premises.evidence_span: a variety of challenges classified into 10 levels of difficulty

premises.text: Companies contribute real anonymized datasets and problems so hackers can build and benchmark algorithms against production-like tasks
premises.evidence_span: inviting companies to give us real data sets or problems that they're actually working on

premises.text: In-browser coding supports compile/test in multiple languages plus bot-vs-bot AI games with visualization and cross-school matchups
premises.evidence_span: you can compile and code right inside our interface

premises.text: Archived challenges release code snippets every two weeks so hackers can learn optimal algorithms from others
premises.evidence_span: archive the challenges every two weeks, and release all the code snippets so that hackers can learn from others
